note: Consumer registry of the evidence feedback loop (design: ~/.claude/references/lse-feedback-loop-design.md §3.8). A participant — a skill, a store, or a write-back tool — is a ROW; adding one changes no code path (INV-7). `references/bridge.md` is RENDERED from these rows by `python loop/runs.py bridge` and never hand-edited (D-L17). `status` is a lifecycle (planned -> live -> retired; retired -> live with a new date and a note); `direction` says how the row participates. Rows are edited by a person with the user's approval, never by a tool. This share's copy keeps the rows portable: three rows for consumer skills this repo does not ship (paper-distill, paper-story, paper-survey-library) are omitted, and the remaining rows' local paths are placeholders — substitute your own before running `loop/runs.py check --registry`.
review_when: a consumer skill is removed or renamed; a preset's contract fields change; a store moves (identity_field / run_pointer); a `planned` row makes its first real call (status -> live, first_seen written by `runs.py check --registry`)

gate_b_verify.purpose: Gate B: verify a method-canon or standard claim before advising

citation_identity.purpose: identity / access-tier / currency verification of a cited source (user-supplied-citations delegation rule; guide §9 step 2)
citation_identity.output_format: caller-specified template: canonical identifier + access tag + one-line relevance + limitations (promotion-table columns)

parameter_lookup.purpose: a literature value for a profile's typical-range cell

consumers.artifact_kind: Source Ledger row (§7b) / user-supplied-citations promotion row

store.identity_field: Identifier cell (free text; the key is derived at read time by idkey.find_all — no migration) ; Canonical identity cell

situations: Gate B verification: SRG fills `gate_b_verify`, consumes the evidence table + run_id, writes the §7b row with `run:<run_id>` in the Verification status cell, then a `consumed` event.
Citation intake or currency pass: one LSE run per profile (`citation_identity`); Checked (date) = the run date; the row cites `run:<run_id>`; the human report stays in ~/.claude/reports/.
A retraction or correction reaches a key its ledger cites: `runs.py affected <key> --scan-srg` names the profile row; SRG re-verifies per guide §3.8 and writes a `correction` event.
Never: SRG's packet -> profile pipeline (guide §9 steps 1, 3–7), profile-lint, eval-impact and routing stay SRG's own.
consumers.why_it_matters_here: The first known caller; it already carries half a loop (Verified (date), review-when, Provenance log) and lacked only the join key and the row->run pointer.
consumers.review_when: domain-expansion-guide.md §3.7/§9 or user-supplied-citations.md Delegation rule change their cells

prior_art_slice.purpose: Phase 1 formal-literature slice: an algorithm's canonical formulation, a reported figure, a standard's wording

consumers.artifact_kind: design-doc prior-art block (hypothesis sheet diff, OSS inventory, borrow ledger)

store.identity_field: citation text (DOI / arXiv in the borrow ledger row)

situations: A sub-problem hinges on published scholarly work: delegate that slice with `prior_art_slice`; OSS inventory, competitors and environment stay in PDT.
After the design ships: a `consumed` event per cited run, artifact = the design doc path + B-n row.
consumers.why_it_matters_here: Its prior-art sweep is the second standing caller (references/prior-art-sweep.md); a patent channel exists that it did not know about.

store.identity_field: DOI ; preprint archiveID (`arXiv:` prefix) ; extra line `arXiv: …` ; ISBN

situations: Join only: `runs.py affected <key>` lists the Zotero item keys whose DOI/arXiv normalize to the key, with their PDF state; duplicates are reported for the user to merge in Zotero, never merged here.
consumers.why_it_matters_here: The user's library is the local corpus and the join target; Ow 2010 sat in it twice with case-different DOIs.
consumers.review_when: Zotero changes its schema or the library path moves (connectors/registry.json zotero_local entry)

consumers.artifact_kind: retraction events (Crossref update-to / relation over the Zotero DOIs)

store.path: (tool not built — credibility-rubric.md §3b names the rule)

situations: When built (needs a known-retracted and a known-good DOI as fixtures, OQ-5): after the Zotero close-out, every fired DOI becomes `python loop/reflux.py retraction --actor a3-retraction-sweep --key doi:… --evidence "<Crossref update-to notice>"` — the same path a person uses.
consumers.why_it_matters_here: Registered before it exists so its event kind and actor id are fixed; a sweep printing '0 retractions' is not believed until calibrated two-sided.
consumers.review_when: the sweep tool ships (status -> live) or Crossref changes its retraction fields

term_check.purpose: annotator: is this the standard term?

prior_results.purpose: annotator: what did earlier work report on this claim

situations: The extensibility demonstration (design §3.8.3): this row is the ENTIRE wiring on the LSE side; PaperLens reads the generated bridge section, fills a preset, receives run_id + keys, writes `consumed` events with its annotation id, and `runs.py affected` later lists those ids when a key is retracted.
consumers.why_it_matters_here: A consumer that does not exist yet, wired by one row — the proof that adding a participant is a registry change, not a code path.
consumers.review_when: PaperLens makes its first real call (status -> live) or its store/identity field is defined
